concepts.definition: A foundational claim is a commitment or hypothesis and has exactly one standing: recovered, an adopted premise consolidating named source rules without treating them as proof; independent, an adopted premise argued by a case where other commitments hold and it fails; derived, a consequence with its premises named; or hypothesis, established by no method clause or argument, not law and retained for falsification. This differs from what a result establishes about its predicate and from a successor's disposition of a predecessor claim.

grounding.quote: Each has exactly one of four standings:

concepts.label: Foundational standing

concepts.definition: Four distinct meanings of join: categorical join is a map between categories; composition boundary joins successive steps; result join combines closed results under one decision rule; relation join is an equality join of participants in an enclosing relation. Unqualified join in a result context means result join.

grounding.quote: Four uses of "join" in this corpus are distinct

concepts.label: Distinct join meanings

concepts.definition: Subject is the exact thing a claim, representation or transformation concerns, specified by inventory and bytes or semantic addresses. Representation is bytes, text, model or program standing for it; equal representations do not establish equal meaning. Interpretation is a declared representation-to-meaning contract stating reliable distinctions and residuals within a Context, whose declared scope includes subject, definitions, basis and admissible observations.

grounding.quote: | Interpretation | a declared contract from representation to meaning within a context; says which distinctions a consumer may rely on and which are residual | P1 |

concepts.label: Subject, representation, interpretation and context

concepts.definition: Outcome U is a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval against which transformation adequacy is judged. Object O is a subject with scoped identity (authority, kind, value), boundary, current state and declared material relations; identity survives admissible state and encoding change.

grounding.quote: | Outcome U | a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval; adequacy of a transformation is judged against it | P2 |

concepts.label: Outcome U and Object O

concepts.definition: Actor performs a step within a capability envelope of context, attention, time and capability; roles are occupied relations selected by configuration, not actor kinds. Step is a bounded unit comprising intake, selected context, grant, execution and output. A step-produced fact is a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be reacquired from declared sources; reproducible observations are excluded.

grounding.quote: | Step | one bounded unit of work: intake, selected context, grant, execution, output | P0 |

concepts.label: Actor, step and step-produced fact

concepts.definition: Claim is an assertion with subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier. Evidence is exact admitted observations or artifacts carrying provenance, subject identity, basis and scope; availability in a frame confers neither semantic truth nor decision authority. Judgment is a recorded evaluation over an unchanged subject with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation. Residual is material uncertainty, omission, loss or unproven relation remaining until authorised disposition.

grounding.quote: | Claim | an assertion with subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier | P6 |

concepts.label: Claim, evidence, judgment and residual

concepts.definition: Basis is the exact state binding a step, claim, result or evaluation, including every material version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration and evidence coordinate. It is immutable or moving with declared advancement detection and reevaluation conditions; mixed bases require an explicit composite relation. Materiality is evaluation-relative: lawful change can change a result, invalidate its basis, change admissible evidence, change who may perform a material operation, or change who may decide an evaluation or material operation; uncertainty and closure are material on the same grounds.

grounding.quote: materiality is evaluation-relative, so a relation material in one frame may be irrelevant in another

concepts.label: Basis and materiality

concepts.definition: Evaluation is a declared question with known admissible result family, evidence basis, decision authority and operation authority where material action occurs; it may seek judgment, prediction, construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification or action recommendation. An evaluation family needs the same material-relation manifold, authority basis and result algebra; similar wording is insufficient.

grounding.quote: similar wording does not prove that two evaluations share a family

concepts.label: Evaluation and evaluation family

concepts.definition: Workspace is the bounded material reasoned over or acted on, potentially including constitutional sources, assets, designs, implementations, tools, runtime, evidence, history, dependencies and human decisions; a repository is only one possible carrier. Material-relation manifold is the finite jointly interpretable variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities, observations and exclusions an evaluation family needs; charts may overlap and imply neither geometric mathematics nor runtime abstraction. Coordinate is the complete locally required basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority position. Topology is the visible relation structure of entities, capabilities, authorities, lifecycle state spaces, adjacencies and seams at one basis, not necessarily the whole workspace.

grounding.quote: no geometric mathematics or runtime abstraction is implied

concepts.label: Workspace, manifold, coordinate and topology

concepts.definition: Capability envelope specifies competence, context capacity, tools, access, applicable evaluation or assurance independence, and configuration required for activation and evaluation. Reference frame is a finite specification of attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations for one declared evaluation family over a stated basis. Activated frame binds a declaration to exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; declaration reuse is not proof of activation correctness.

grounding.quote: a reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct

concepts.label: Reference frame, activation and capability envelope

concepts.definition: Frame set is the human-declared available family for an outcome or workspace, potentially with overlaps, alternatives, specialist, exploratory and separately activated assurance frames; it need not be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology. Active configuration consists of frame activations and declared result relations for one evaluation or decision, whether one frame or multiple disjoint, overlapping or composed frames. Lens is a reusable question family; abstract authority, capability and reuse, temporal behaviour, transport and proof may be lenses. Role allocates responsibility or admitted authority; persona changes approach or salience; abstraction hides or contracts detail; component is a structural subject part. None is a reference frame by identity alone.

grounding.quote: one component may appear in several frames and one frame may cross several components

concepts.label: Frame set, configuration, lens, role, persona, abstraction and component

concepts.definition: Authority is identity-bearing permission to operate or dispose acceptance within scope. Its distinct kinds are frame-set authority, the human authority declaring or accepting a project frame set; semantic authority, owner of a material relation's meaning; evaluation authority, role permitted to evaluate; operation authority, owner-issued grant to construct, transform, admit, publish or mutate a material subject; and decision authority, role permitted to accept, reject or otherwise dispose a result. Actor identity identifies the human, agent, tool or process and is not authority.

grounding.quote:
These may coincide in a lawful case and
never collapse by default.
an identity-bearing permission to operate or to dispose acceptance within a scope

concepts.label: Authority kinds

concepts.definition: An explicitly admitted bounded proxy may exercise human authority where governing identity and authority law permits; its identity remains distinct from human-authority identity and its action stays inside the existing grant.

grounding.quote: A proxy acts only inside its existing grant.

concepts.label: Bounded human-authority proxy

concepts.definition: Frame disjointness is structural absence of shared material variables, coordinates, evidence or result dependencies for declared evaluations. Evaluation independence is separate activation without consumption or influence of one another's unclosed working results; shared subjects, overlapping manifolds and later conjunction of closed results are permitted. Assurance independence is claim-relative non-authorship, evidence acquisition, reference exposure, actor and configuration separation required by governing assurance law.

grounding.quote: Three relations stay distinct

concepts.label: Structural disjointness, evaluation independence and assurance independence

concepts.definition: Reference frame F is ⟨Q,B,M,C,I,A,E,X,R,J,K,D⟩: evaluation family; workspace and topology basis; material-relation manifold; coordinate/equality law; applicable invariants; authority relation; admissible evidence/provenance law; exclusions/prohibited assumptions; closed result algebra or refinement into it; invalidation/rechart condition; actor capability envelope; optional dependencies, overlaps, inputs and outputs involving other frames. It specifies an evaluation contract's finite attention scope, not a mandatory schema or runtime carrier.

grounding.quote: A reference frame F is the tuple ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩

concepts.label: Frame tuple

Source project is the mutable workspace building the next cut. Release cut is an immutable annotated release-candidate boundary over a published feature set. Product is the released immutable thing resulting from acceptance of that cut. Install is a stamped workspace instance of that Product. Artifact is published output built by a source project or configured install. object with its own identity

concepts.definition: The boundary around a probabilistic, agentic or delegated work unit has six parts that live specification and design should declare: input/output contract; required context; capability or role expectation; admissible evidence and evaluator regime; provenance obligation; lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion states. the

concepts.label: Declared work boundary

concepts.definition: Construction realises a selected outer contract through steps. Its algorithmic account describes steps; informational account declares data meaning under an Interpretation; computational account describes how people, machines or combinations execute it in a declared environment, with build-tenant environment supplied by SPEC_METHOD §11. These accounts are distinct for every construction, independent of corpus tiers, and any construction may need all three.

grounding.quote:
Three accounts of a construction stay
distinct

concepts.label: Three construction accounts

concepts.definition: Semantic import is reference-only adoption of an owner's meaning unchanged, directed from named source to importing context, with identical owner-qualified meanings, no loss, translation or ownership transfer and no conferred authority. Adoption is a target taking an imported concept into use under source-owned adoption premises; lifecycle remains source-owned.

grounding.quote:
An import is
reference-only.

concepts.label: Semantic import and adoption

concepts.definition: P0 Bounded construction is recovered: finite actors realise a selected outer contract through steps whose selected contexts fit their envelopes; internal paths remain their own. Premises include selected outcome, potentially different successive actors, reacquisition of declared sources but not private memory, non-reacquirable step-produced facts, an open world and candidate status of outputs until evaluated. Named finite-attention, sufficiency, closure, work-boundary and refinement rules are sources, not proof.

grounding.quote: | P0 Bounded construction | recovered | the actor's internal path within a step is its own |

concepts.label: P0 Bounded construction

concepts.definition: P1 Interpretation is an independent adopted premise: subject, representation and interpretation differ; meaning holds within declared context through a declared contract, and structural success never establishes fidelity. Its non-entailment example preserves other commitments while a downstream step silently reads a typed length written in feet as metres. Algorithmic means explicit and structurally checkable; lawful semantic decision requires an exact decision contract.

grounding.quote: P1 Interpretation. Subject, representation and interpretation are distinct;

concepts.label: P1 Interpretation

concepts.definition: P2 Purpose is independent: selected outcome defines adequacy and interfaces inherit material obligations from the transformation they serve; an obligation with no route to the outcome is unjustified. Its non-entailment case preserves other commitments while interface obligations follow available capacity instead of transformation purpose, yielding the same alleged adequacy for opposite outcomes.

grounding.quote:
P2 Purpose. A selected outcome defines adequacy; interfaces inherit
material obligations from the transformation they serve.

concepts.label: P2 Purpose

concepts.definition: P3 Identity is independent: identity is declared as (authority, kind, value), survives admissible change, and a boundary is a claim with a proof obligation. Current state, historical observation and representation identity remain separate. Its non-entailment case preserves other commitments while location substitutes for declared identity, so moving an object splits it into two apparent objects.

grounding.quote:
P3 Identity. An object's identity is declared (authority, kind, value) and
survives admissible change; a boundary is a claim with a proof obligation.

concepts.label: P3 Identity

concepts.definition: P4a Typed composition is independent: steps compose only when the first result type and judgment satisfy the second's exact declared domain and preconditions; composition retains both identities, intermediate results, judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states. The non-entailment case lets a second step run on every output and return invalid_basis outside its domain while retaining only outer-contract-needed facts: other commitments hold but admission and intermediate-state preservation fail. Retained intermediate results and stop states locate repair or restart after falsification or resumption.

grounding.quote:
P4a Typed composition. Two steps compose only when the first's result type
and judgment satisfy the second's exact declared domain and preconditions.

concepts.label: P4a Typed composition

concepts.definition: P4b Conservation of step-produced facts derives from P0 and P2, specifically non-reacquirability: the producing step records judgments, residuals, observations and authority decisions needed by the outer contract because later actors cannot reacquire private results. Reacquirable sources instead follow sufficiency. The source reframes nine predecessor conservation statements as one obligation with scoped instances for authority, residual, judgment, frame, transition, successor claim and evidence by reference.

grounding.quote:
P4b Conservation of step-produced facts. Judgments, residuals, observations
and authority decisions the outer contract needs are recorded by the step
that produced them.

concepts.label: P4b Conservation of step-produced facts

concepts.definition: P5 Totality derives from P0's open-world premise and P6: a step may encounter a condition outside its context but cannot report success on it; its algebra therefore has first-class non-success outcomes and its control model names the next move. Choosing precisely indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis is a declared choice owned by Results, not entailed merely by this derivation.

grounding.quote:
That these
outcomes are three, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis, is a
declared choice

concepts.label: P5 Totality

concepts.definition: P6 Justification and authority is independent: definitions, assumptions, observations, candidate judgments and accepted claims have distinct standing; evidence supports a claim on a basis, while authority permits or disposes within scope. Neither evidence nor authority is minted by the other. Its non-entailment case is an otherwise compliant bounded actor treating a green label as acceptance.

grounding.quote:
P6 Justification and authority. Definitions, assumptions, observations,
candidate judgments and accepted claims have distinct standing;

concepts.label: P6 Justification and authority

concepts.definition: Construction synthesis relates P0–P6 to movement from observed current state toward acceptable destination under finite resources. It is a derived consequence, not another commitment, and the source calls it law carried from common requirements. P0 bounds acquisition/work while preserving internal strategy; P1 distinguishes required conditions, observations and predictions while preserving comparative meaning; P2 supplies destination Z and adequacy; P3 separates persistent subject, observations and dependencies from accounts; P4a carries obligations across steps/refinement/boundaries; P4b conserves non-reacquirable products through observation, correction and reuse; P5 accounts for resource tradeoffs, recursive progress, recovery and truthful undecided stops; P6 establishes support and authority to change models, act or accept.

grounding.quote:
It is derived, not a further
commitment

concepts.label: Construction synthesis

concepts.definition: A deciding-rule family groups related rules deciding outcomes; it is material when those outcomes matter to the selected method outcome. Its owner-local entry table traces instance premises and one row per consequence using five columns: premises with standing; consequence; linked owning rule; only the added domain/policy choice and its owner or none; and Pillar contributions. Neither table nor consumer trace owns rules or choices, supplies additional determinations, or proves every named rule clause.

grounding.quote: | Premises, with standing | Consequence that follows | Rule in this member that states it | Added domain or policy choice, and its owner | Pillar |

concepts.label: Foundation-to-law family trace

concepts.definition: Pillars are the Product-owned Foundational Reduction's ordered contributions: 1 specification/project structure; 2 world models, identity and Markov objects; 3 algebraic calculus; 4 functional design; 5 outcome-driven development; 6 information/interpretation; 7 reference frames; 8 computational calculus/execution binding; 9 evidence/correction/authority; 10 axiomatic calculus. A Pillar cell is only a trace: no premise, standing, choice ownership or claim of axiomatic status or derivation from finite capacity.

grounding.quote: A Pillar cell is a trace, like the rest of the table:

concepts.label: Pillar contribution trace

concepts.definition: The family index records each family's table locus, accounted-for members/sections and union of table-row Pillar cells. It decides nothing. A table-pending row identifies intended locus and members but traces no rules; a pending Pillar cell names no pillar until the table supplies that column. The index also gives explicit reasons for sections without family tables.

nothing: each rule is in its owning section, and each trace is in its
table

concepts.definition: The subject's algebra describes typed step composition, conservation accounting, reference sufficiency, explicit latitude, commonisation candidates and the demonstrations needed for categorical claims. These are descriptions of source-defined operations and proof obligations, not operations performed by this interpretation.
